topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture with administrative framing, the lecturer's background, and the primary learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Environmental Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of cancer development by contrasting intrinsic random mutations with environmental exposures and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive malignant transformation, focusing on chronic infection and the mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Carcinogens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical compounds interact with host metabolic processes to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on how promotional signaling, chronic inflammation, and host developmental timing permit tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Determining Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental strategies used to detect and demonstrate carcinogenic effects.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with framing remarks on evaluating carcinogen potency, exposure, and daily risk-benefit decisions.
